name: Pop Art (supplemental design reference, not a directly named style in the source collection).
visualIdentity: Explicit cues: mass-culture objects, comic imagery, repeated panels, bold color fields, heavy outlines, and optional halftones. Lettering is part of the composition. Repetition, color substitution, scale changes, and split screens surround one clear focal image. Comic imagery or halftones alone do not establish Pop Art.
suitableUses: Explicit: the source says Pop Art alone suits single iconic images. Its suggested combinations list product promos, campaign headlines, event teasers, music promos, and social loops as best-fit uses. Other uses are unspecified.
limitations: Thin type, halftones over letterforms, and strobe-like full color swaps are to be avoided. Red must never carry small text, and too many simultaneous words should be avoided. Gradients are disabled by default. The palette is a suggestion, and approved exact colors override it. Two-color contrast checks do not guarantee readability over images, textures, or video.
palette: Suggested only, for new artwork when no approved palette is supplied: background #FFF6D6, foreground #171717, accent_1 #E8393E red, accent_2 #F1C932 yellow, accent_3 #2671C6 blue, with heavy dark outlines. Foreground on background measures 16.566:1. Accent_1 (4.342:1) is decorative fill only. Recheck every pairing on composited frames.
motionAndInteraction: Motion should be smooth and coherent where it benefits the action. Deliberate sharp cuts, impacts, constant-speed sections, and reading holds should be preserved, and not every transition needs easing. Video state must derive from composition time, not live input. Motion references 012, 013, and 015 are optional and must pass scene-fit screening; choosing none is valid.
audio: Audio is unspecified as a requirement; the source imposes no fixed genre, tempo, voice, or mandatory layer. Options include background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence, chosen per topic. Music promos may use beat-timed color swaps. Interactive audio should be user-started, not autoplay, and speech must stay intelligible.
assetRequirements: Prepare color separations, comic contours, and repeated panels before implementation. Halftones should be generated stably in Canvas, while SVG or HTML text stays crisp. Load fonts and assets before rendering. Subject, exact copy, duration, aspect ratio, resolution, frame rate, audio needs, and output directory are unspecified and must be supplied or stated as assumptions. Approved colors and source artwork override suggested tokens.
combinations: Style-093 (bold lettering and onomatopoeia motion) suits product promos and campaign headlines. Keep lettering outlined in #171717, use one focal image per frame, and avoid halftones over letters. Style-105 (beat timing) suits music promos and loops. Cycle color swaps only among palette tokens, stagger panel changes, keep the halftone pattern fixed, and avoid autoplay audio.
productionApproach: Style renderer: SVG for outlines, masks, and clipping, and Canvas 2D for stable halftones, with an optional luminance halftone shader. Motion engine: GSAP for a paused, seekable timeline, with Motion or mo.js as optional layers only after deterministic seeking is verified. Pipeline: HyperFrames is primary for assembly, timing, and export. Remotion is fallback only when HyperFrames cannot meet a verified requirement. Verify opening, action, transition, and closing frames, full playback, audio sync, and loop seams.
